Source says: Norges Bank (Norway). AKO Capital owned or ran an asset held by officials of Norges Bank (Norway). In August 2020 Norges Bank's Executive Board revised incoming NBIM chief executive Nicolai Tangen's employment terms to reduce conflict-of-interest concerns raised by the Storting's Standing Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs: Tangen would divest his holding in AKO Capital LLP and transfer his holding and dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation, with no ownership interest in AKO Capital in perpetuity, and would hold all his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said there had been a breach of guidelines, regulations and laws in Tangen's appointment. Executive Board chair Oystein Olsen said the board had believed the existing contractual framework was sufficient but acknowledged the Storting took a different view. Tangen could take office on 1 September. NBIM revises Nicolai Tangen terms following conflict of interest concerns (European Pensions)

current_paragraph: The State Tribunal is the court in Warsaw that tries senior Polish officials for breaking the law in office. In October 2026 the Sejm's Committee on Constitutional Responsibility backed a report supporting the referral of National Bank of Poland president Adam Glapinski to it, and the Sejm Marshal said the full chamber would vote in the second half of November 2026. The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses Glapinski of indirectly financing the budget deficit through asset purchases in 2020 and 2021 and of acting without proper authorisation for those purchases and for currency interventions. He and the bank called the allegations baseless, and nothing is proven.

current_paragraph: The Directorate of Public Prosecutions, in Gaborone, brings criminal cases on behalf of the state in Botswana. Headed by Stephen Tiroyakgosi, it called in Moses Pelaelo, Governor of the Bank of Botswana, to hear his account of 100 billion pula that the state alleged had been looted from the central bank by former president Ian Khama and former intelligence chief Isaac Kgosi. Those allegations are unproven. Tiroyakgosi said Pelaelo told them no money is missing from the Bank of Botswana, and that the investigation was continuing.

current_paragraph: The Sejm is the lower house of Poland's parliament, based in Warsaw. It is handling the case against Adam Glapiński, president of the National Bank of Poland, the central bank. Ruling coalition members of parliament filed a motion in March 2024 to send him to the State Tribunal, a court that can try senior officials, with eight accusations. current_paragraph: The Supreme Court of Thailand, in Bangkok, is named in a case involving the Bank of Thailand. A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis. On 5 October 2016 the Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case. He was cleared.
